hook: A USCENTCOM Mission Report (MISREP) from the 50th Attack Squadron documenting two separate UAP observations made during a 20-hour, 43-minute Joint Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JSR) mission over the Persian Gulf on October 24, 2023, under Operation Spartan Shield.
why_it_matters: This report is notable for documenting two distinct UAP events within 41 minutes of each other during a single operational ISR sortie, with the second contact moving at a higher estimated velocity (440 MPH) than the first (320 MPH). Both sightings were formally entered into AARO's reporting structure with structured data fields, demonstrating the DoD's standardized UAP intake process in action during an active operational context that also included a live Iranian Air Defense guard call. The concurrent collection of SIGINT and IMINT during the mission means UAP observations occurred in an environment with multiple sensor modalities active, though none are reported as having interrogated the objects.

key_findings.finding: Two UAP events were formally logged during a single mission, 41 minutes apart, both while the aircraft was at FL243 on a 280-degree trajectory at 162 KTAS.

quotes.text: AT 02412,[iiuOBSERVED IX UAP. SEE UAP LINE I.
AT 03222,[iii]OBSERVED IX UAP. SEE UAP LINE 2.

• Friendly Aircraft Altitude/Depth: FL243
• Friendly Aircraft Trajectory: 280 DEGREES

key_findings.finding: The first UAP registered a cold thermal signature on infrared sensors and was estimated moving at 320 MPH, assessed by the observer as Benign and not under intelligent control.

quotes.text: • UAP Under Intelligent Control (yes/no; if yes, describe): NO

key_findings.finding: The second UAP, detected 41 minutes after the first and near a similar grid location, was estimated at 440 MPH — faster than the first contact — but its thermal signature was listed as UNK, and it was also assessed as Benign and not under intelligent control.

quotes.text: • UAP Under Intelligent Control (yes/no; if yes, describe): NO

key_findings.finding: Iranian Air Defense issued a professional guard call to the aircraft during the mission, warning it to maintain safe distance from the border; the aircraft responded it was conducting routine operations in international airspace.

quotes.text: RECEIVED IX GUARD CALL FROM IRANIAN AIR DEFENSE STATING "MAINTAIN SAFE DISTANCE FROM BORDER". CALL WAS PROFESSIONAL. ~RESPONDED "THIS IS A COALITION AIRCRAFT CONDUCTING ROUTINE OPERATIONS IN INTERNATIONAL AIRSPACE".

key_findings.finding: The mission simultaneously conducted SIGINT collection and IMINT operations for over 16 hours under Operation Spartan Shield, and the Full Motion Video (FMV) from the mission was subsequently exploited by DGS-2.

quotes.text: FROM 01502 TO 2019Z, ~ COLLECTED SIGINT VlA AIRHANDLER.
FROM 01552 TO 1837Z,[iji]CONDUCTED IMINT ISO OP SPARTAN SHIELD
AT 2058Z, ~ LANDED AT OMAM. FMV WAS EXPLOITED BYDGS-2.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The report is explicitly approved for release to AARO and uses AARO's standardized UAP reporting fields (event type, physical state, maneuverability, intelligent control, signatures), making AARO the direct institutional recipient and processor of this report.

The aircraft identified itself as a 'COALITION AIRCRAFT' during the Iranian guard call, suggesting multinational context, though no specific allied partner intelligence sharing is documented in the text.
